{{Quote|Keep your peace-loving ways to ''yourself'', Chirpa! I was born to ''conquer!''<nowiki />|Graak|<ref name="Ewoks 4" />}}
'''Graak''' was an [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] who was banished from [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]] for disobeying its law too many times. During his [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]], he met a group of the [[Lizard Warrior]] [[Species/Legends|species]], and after he [[Teacher/Legends|taught]] them fighting skills, they asked him to be their leader. In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the [[Lizard/Legends|lizards]] captured two [[Youngling/Legends|young]] Ewoks, [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket Warrick]] and [[Teebo/Legends|Teebo]], and brought them to a [[Cave/Legends|cave]] where Graak was located.

After trying to escape, the Ewoks were quickly recaptured by Graak. Warrick revealed to Teebo who Graak really was and why he had been banished. He explained to the Ewoks that the only way they would be permitted to go free would be for them to survive being [[Hunting/Legends|hunted]] by Graak and the Lizard Warriors. Even though Graak refused to give them weapons of any kind, the Ewoks were able to fend off the warriors. They found the end of the [[Valley of the Lizard Warriors|valley]] that Graak and the Lizard Warriors occupied and prepared to go home to Bright Tree Village.

Graak, however, had been awaiting them, and he began to fight with Warrick. He was able to overpower the young [[Scout/Legends|scout]], but just before he could defeat Warrick, he was interrupted by the leader of the Lizard Warriors, [[Joddar]], who threatened Graak with a [[Spear/Legends|spear]]; Joddar had turned on the Ewok after Warrick and Teebo had taught him compassion. He then told Graak that he would be allowed to stay in the valley if he wished, but no longer as his leader. Graak declined and went his own way.

==Biography==
===A naughty Ewok===
{{Quote|You have ''disobeyed'' the law for the last time, Graak! We do not fight except in self-defense!|Chief Chirpa|<ref name="Ewoks 4" />}}
[[File:GraakChirpa.png|thumb|left|260px|Graak (far right) was exiled by Chief Chirpa (far left).]]
[[Standard year/Legends|Years]] before<ref name="Ewoks 4" /> [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{InsiderCite|23|Star Wars Publications Timeline|''Star Wars'' Publications Timeline}} dates the events of the [[Star Wars: Ewoks (1985)|''Ewoks'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]], which include the events of [[Ewoks (1985) 4|''Ewoks'' 4]], to three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], which corresponds to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> Graak lived on the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]] as part of an [[Bright Tree Village tribe|Ewok tribe]]. He disobeyed the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] law enough times that he was [[Prisoner/Legends|arrested]] and brought before [[Chirpa/Legends|Chirpa]], the [[Chief/Legends|Chief]] of [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]]. Chirpa pointed at Graak, chastising him for fighting in instances other than self-defense. Graak insisted that he was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] to conquer, and that Chirpa could keep his peace-loving ways for himself.<ref name="Ewoks 4" />

Chirpa told Graak that his desires would not be fulfilled in Bright Tree Village, and [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|banished]] him from there to the [[Valley of the Lizard Warriors]]. He invited Graak to live as he wished there, mentioning that heaven should help him. He was then led away by an Ewok armed with a [[Spear/Legends|spear]]. Graak's tale would eventually be told to the Ewok [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket Wystri Warrick]]. Around that [[Time/Legends|point]], Graak met the [[Lizard Warrior]] [[Joddar]] along with Joddar's men. He [[Teacher/Legends|taught]] the Lizard Warriors fighting skills, and in gratitude, they asked him to become their leader.<ref name="Ewoks 4" />

===Capturing the Ewoks===
{{Quote|Teebo! Look! He's....''"<br />"''Yes..an ''Ewok'', just as you both are!|Wicket Warrick and Graak|<ref name="Ewoks 4" />}}
[[File:GraakWhip.png|thumb|right|275px|Graak's identity was discovered by Wicket Warrick (far left).]]
In 3 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]],<ref name="Date" /> Warrick and fellow [[Youngling/Legends|young]] Ewok [[Teebo/Legends|Teebo]] were attempting to walk home from a mission when they were captured by Joddar's men, who took them to a [[Cave/Legends|cave]] where Graak was located. Warrick and Teebo were both surprised to see a fellow Ewok there, which Graak acknowledged. Teebo expressed his delight to see Graak, and Warrick asked who the warriors were. Graak told the [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] to rest and enjoy his hospitality, and that their questions would eventually be answered. The Ewoks thanked him as he walked away.<ref name="Ewoks 4" />

Joddar began to converse with Graak, asking if they were ready to begin. Graak cut him off, warning him not to give them away, but it was too late, as Warrick had heard Joddar say Graak's name. Knowing Graak's past, Warrick convinced Teebo to sneak away from the cave. However, as they ran away, Graak used a [[Capturing stick|whip-like weapon]] to recapture the Ewoks, laughing at their attempt to get away. Warrick then revealed to Teebo Graak's exile, and their captor claimed that he was honored that Warrick knew of him. Warrick shot back that Chirpa had never spoke of Graak with honor, which reminded Graak of what he had only ever perceived as cowardice from Chirpa.<ref name="Ewoks 4" />

===The Ewok hunt===
{{Quote|Yes! ''Survival'' of the ''fittest''! Prepare for the ''hunt'', my Ewok friends!|Graak|<ref name="Ewoks 4" />}}
[[File:GraakHunt.png|thumb|left|300px|Graak hunted Warrick and Teebo.]]
Graak recounted his banishment, remembering it as though it had occurred just the previous [[Standard day/Legends|day]]. Following his story, he told the Ewoks that due to their passing through his valley, they would need to obey his laws. He told them to prepare for the [[Hunting/Legends|hunt]] and proceeded to explain it: the Ewoks would be hunted as though they were [[Species/Legends|animals]]. They would only be allowed to go free if they reached the end of the valley safely. In order to keep the hunt fair, Graak allowed the Ewoks a head start to a [[totem pole]] that stood close by. Warrick, also in the interest of a fair hunt, asked if they would receive weapons to defend themselves with. Graak laughed, claiming that peace-loving people had no need for weapons.<ref name="Ewoks 4" />

After reaching the pole, Warrick and Teebo were barraged with spears by the Lizard Warriors. Graak watched as two of the warriors chased them near a cliff. As the warriors prepared to attack Teebo with their spears, Warrick rolled a [[Tree/Legends|tree]] [[Wood/Legends|trunk]] at them that caused them to fall into the [[Water/Legends|river]] below. The Ewoks then tried to run away, with Graak ordering the Lizard Warriors to chase after them. Warrick and Teebo were able to launch [[burr ball]]s<ref name="Ewoks 4" />&mdash;a type of [[Berry/Legends|berry]]<ref name="SWG">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=item|Burr Ball}}</ref>&mdash;at them, which caused the [[Lizard/Legends|lizards]] enough pain to run away. Graak cursed the Ewoks, explaining to Joddar that they were more cunning than he expected. Joddar vowed that he would stop them or [[Death/Legends|die]] trying.<ref name="Ewoks 4" />

[[File:GraakJoddar.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Graak and Joddar]]
Joddar was unsuccessful, as he was nearly [[Diet/Legends|eaten]] by an [[Endorian swamp beast]], with Warrick and Teebo saving him. Warrick explained to him that part of their choice to save him was to show that not all Ewoks were like Graak. In order to repay them, Joddar pointed the Ewoks towards the end of the valley. He bid them goodbye, warning them to be wary of Graak. Indeed, as they ran toward the edge of the valley, Graak, who had been hiding behind a [[Bush/Legends|bush]], again used his [[Whip (weapon)|whip]]-like weapon to trip them up, catching and choking Teebo by his neck. He explained that while together, the Ewoks may have had a chance against him, when split apart, he had the advantage. Warrick asked him to let Teebo go, maintaining that they were finished with his hunt.<ref name="Ewoks 4" />

===Graak vs. the Ewoks===
{{Quote|You see, that is why you will ''never'' win! You play by the ''rules''!''"<br />"''Then I'll play&hellip;by ''your'' rules!|Graak and Warrick|<ref name="Ewoks 4" />}}
[[File:WicketChokesGraak.png|thumb|left|260px|Graak is choked by Warrick.]]
Graak pointed out that that was the Ewoks' weakness&mdash;they always played by the rules. As though to prove him wrong, Warrick picked up a two-pronged stick and knocked Graak off his [[Limb/Legends|feet]], pinning his neck against the ground and choking him. Graak begged him to stop, with Warrick only doing so after Graak gave his word that he would allow Warrick and Teebo to leave. However, after being released, Graak immediately broke the truce and threw a handful of dirt in Warrick's [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. While the young Ewok attempted to regain his vision, Graak told him that he should have finished him when he had the opportunity, and that the difference between them was that he had a "killer instinct."<ref name="Ewoks 4" />

Just as Graak was about to smash a large rock on Warrick, Joddar arrived and poked his back with a spear, ordering him to stop. He told him that the Ewoks were free to go due to their surviving the hunt, but Graak felt that Joddar had gone too far. He rhetorically asked Joddar if he was not his leader, but Joddar suggested that perhaps the young scouts would do a better job than Graak, as they had taught him something that Graak never had. Graak scoffed, asking what the Ewoks could have taught. Joddar responded that he had learned compassion, and how to help others in need. He told Graak that he would allow for him to stay in the valley, but Graak declined, saying that he cared not for weakness and that he would go his own way, which he did. Graak shared his name with<ref name="Ewoks 4" /> the Ewok [[Deity/Legends|spirit]] [[Graak (spirit)|Graak]].<ref name="GCG">''[[Galactic Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|You should have ''finished'' me when you had the chance! But then&hellip; that is the ''difference'' between you and me&hellip; you lack&hellip; the ''killer instinct!''<nowiki />|Graak to Wicket Warrick|<ref name="Ewoks 4" />}}
[[File:GraakChokesTeebo.png|thumb|right|300px|Graak attemps to choke Teebo.]]
Graak felt that he was born to conquer, which resulted in his breaking Ewok law to the point that he was banished. He regarded Chief Chirpa as cowardly, and the [[Council of Elders (Ewok)/Legends|Ewok council]] as a group of "buffoons." During his exile, he was able to convince the Lizard Warriors to take him as their leader for his teaching them fighting skills. After he captured Warrick and Teebo, Graak pretended to be hospitable, asking that they relax and enjoy the [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]]. Graak was willing to hunt young Ewoks even without supplying them with weapons to defend themselves, citing their desire for peace as reasoning for their not needing such tools.<ref name="Ewoks 4" />

Regardless, the Ewoks were able to escape the hunt, which Graak had dubbed the "survival of the fittest," surprising the criminal. At the end of the hunt, Warrick assumed that Graak would relent as they had survived. However, Graak refused to play by his own rules, pointing out that the fact that the Ewoks did play fairly was the reason that they would never win. He further proved that he would not follow any type of rules when he went against his promise to give up after Warrick held his neck to the ground, instead throwing dirt in the Ewok's eyes. He felt that his "killer instinct" was a trait that the Ewoks lacked.<ref name="Ewoks 4" />

When Joddar intervened to save Warrick from Graak, Graak was surprised, and scoffed when Joddar explained that the Ewoks had taught him compassion. Afterward, Graak walked away, saying that he cared little for weakness and would go his own way. He was an Ewok with [[Color/Legends|blue]] [[Hair/Legends|fur]]<ref name="Ewoks 4" /> who stood taller than 1.32 [[Meter/Legends|meters]].<ref name="height" />

==Skills and abilities==
{{Quote|That's when I met ''Joddar'' and his men and taught them new, deadly fighting skills! In gratitude they asked me to ''lead'' them!|Graak|<ref name="Ewoks 4" />}}
Graak was able to teach fighting skills to the Lizard Warriors. While he was skilled enough in battle to capture the Ewoks on multiple occasions, they were able to defeat him as he underestimated their abilities.<ref name="Ewoks 4" />

==Equipment==
Graak wore purple [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]] with an orange [[Cape/Legends|cape]]. The portion of the cape that draped over his head had white horns, and his wrists had orange cuffs on them. He also wore a black [[Eye patch/Legends|eye patch]] over his right eye and a [[Belt/Legends|belt]] on his waist. He used a whip-like weapon to successfully capture Warrick and Teebo twice.<ref name="Ewoks 4" />

==Behind the scenes==
Graak appeared as the main antagonist in the [[Ewoks (1985) 4|fourth issue]] of the [[Star Wars: Ewoks (1985)|''Ewoks'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]], which was written by [[David Manak]], illustrated by [[Warren Kremer]], and published by [[Marvel Comics]]<ref name="Ewoks 4" /> on [[July 30]], [[1985]]. Earlier that year, Graak was mentioned in the thirty-first issue of Marvel's ''[[Marvel Age]]'' magazine, which previewed ''Ewoks'' 4.<ref name="Marvel">{{BookCite|title=[[Marvel Age]]|number=Vol. 1 No. 31|publisher=[[Marvel Comics]] Group|date=[[October]] [[1985]]|issn=8750-4367}}</ref>
